newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast and donors to discuss debt Friday.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast and donors to discuss debt Friday.

text.p: Ivory Coast will meet International Monetary Fund and World Bank officials in Abidjan on Friday to discuss a debt reduction strategy to be finalised in July, according to an IMF spokesman.
"We will be discussing Expanded Social and Adjustment Facilites (ESAF) and Ivory Coast's debt strategy under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) scheme," Pierre van den Boogaerde told Reuters.
The Abidjan meeting follows the IMF's agreement last month to widen guidelines determining Ivory Coast's eligibility for debt reduction as a Heavily Indebted Poor Country.
Van den Boogaerde said Ivory Coast and the IMF had reached agreement in principle on broadening the eligibility criteria beyond the standard debt-to-exports ratio of 200 percent.
"A PFP (Policy Framework Paper) will be agreed in July at an IMF meeting in Washington," he added. "Discussions will be held around July and we do not foresee any problems."
Ivory Coast's total debt is estimated at $17 billion.

The government on Tuesday signed an accord with the London Club of creditor banks allowing it to slash its external commercial debt to $2.6 billion from $6.8 billion. It has also struck deals with the Paris Club of multilateral lenders.
The amount of debt to be considered under the HIPC programme would be around $4 billion, van den Boogaerde said.

Ivory Coast's economy has recovered after devaluation in 1994 of the CFA franc currency it shares with other Francophone countries in Africa. In 1994, annual Gross Domestic Product growth stood at 1.8 percent. The figure was 6.8 percent in 1996 and a projected 5.6 percent for 1997, according to Boogaerde.
